key_expressions: Do we need a specific format?,

A: Did you submit the assignment?
I uploaded mine, but I’m not sure if it went through properly.
I’m also worried I might have named the file wrong.
B: Yes, I submitted it a little while ago.
If the upload completed normally, it should be fine.
But if you're unsure, it’s safer to open the file again and double-check.

A: The deadline is tonight at 11:59 p.m., right?
I feel like the professor said something different in class.
Did you check the announcement again?
B: Yes, the announcement clearly says 11:59 p.m.
The explanation in class may have been a bit confusing.
But the posted announcement is the official guideline, so follow that time.

A: We’re supposed to submit the file as a PDF, right?
I made mine in Word first and then converted it.
I hope nothing got messed up during the conversion.
B: Yes, PDF is the required format.
It usually converts fine, but tables or images sometimes shift.
It’s best to preview the PDF before you submit it.

A: How did you format your references?
I wasn’t sure whether we needed APA or MLA.
Did the professor specify a style?
B: The professor asked us to use APA format.
I remember seeing that in the slides from the first week.
If you'd like, I can send you the example I organized.

A: Do we need to upload a draft as well?
The wording in the announcement was a bit unclear.
For now, I only uploaded my final version.
B: Drafts are optional, so you don’t have to submit one.
Uploading only the final version is enough to meet the requirements.
But if you want full confirmation, you could email the professor.

A: Do you know if we’re allowed to resubmit?
I noticed a typo right after turning mine in.
Should I delete it and upload a corrected one?
B: Yes, resubmission is allowed.
The system only keeps the most recent upload, so there’s no issue.
If you found a typo, it’s better to fix it and resubmit.

A: Do we also have to upload our presentation slides?
The assignment description said to submit only the written part.
But we’ll need slides for the presentation, right?
B: Slides don’t need to be submitted beforehand.
The professor said we only need to show them during the presentation.
Still, preparing them early will make things easier later.

A: Did you see the grading rubric the professor posted?
It looks more detailed than the previous one.
Do you think that will affect the score a lot?
B: Yes, I checked it earlier.
The categories are more detailed, but the actual weight doesn’t seem to have changed much.
The professor emphasized that clarity of content is the most important factor.

A: Who was in charge of submitting our group assignment?
We’re still finishing the combined file on our side.
Do you think it will be submitted by tonight?
B: Minji was assigned to handle the submission.
I heard she’s organizing the final file right now.
She said she would submit it before tonight, so we should be fine.

A: Wow… I finally finished the assignment!
I felt all the tension leave after clicking the submit button.
I think I deserve a break now.
B: You did great — that must have been a lot of work.
I know the feeling of relief after submitting something big.
Take a good rest today and start fresh tomorrow.
